rules.statement: Destroy key management service keys only through the single remote secret destroyer service, never by calling a provider's key deletion API directly from a caller.
rules.why: One destroyer applies the same skip rules (only generated remote secrets), post-commit token handling, no-throw behavior and failure logging to every destruction.
rules.check: Look for new code that calls a KMS provider's DestroyKeyAsync, ScheduleKeyDeletion or similar deletion API directly instead of going through the destroyer.

rules.statement: Destroying a KMS key after a committed change must not throw back into the caller, must run without the caller's cancellation token on its own bounded token, and must log each failure with the secret id or KMS key id and the provider.
rules.why: The change is already committed, so a failed cleanup must not fail the request, a caller cancellation must not abandon it, and a leftover key must be traceable so the sweep can reclaim it.
rules.check: Check post-commit key destruction code for exceptions that propagate, for use of the request's CancellationToken, and for failure logs missing the key or secret id and provider.

rules.statement: Tag every KMS key a deployment creates with its configured deployment name, and make any sweep or bulk destruction filter on that tag instead of trusting the account, vault or key ring as the scope.
rules.why: Deployments can share an AWS account, Azure Key Vault or Google key ring, so a sweep that trusts the scope would destroy another deployment's keys.
rules.check: Look for key creation that omits the deployment tag or label, and for listing or destruction code that selects keys by group name or location without also matching the deployment tag.

rules.statement: An orphaned-key sweep lists the provider's keys before it reads the stored references, and destroys only keys created at or before now minus a grace period.
rules.why: Listing first means a key recorded during the pass is never swept, and the grace period means a key whose creation is still in flight, before its secret is committed, is never swept.
rules.check: In sweep or garbage-collection code, check that the remote listing happens before the stored-reference read and that a creation-time cutoff with a grace period is applied before destruction.

rules.statement: Skip, never destroy, a remote key whose tags or metadata cannot be read during a sweep.
rules.why: Without readable tags the sweep can't prove the key belongs to this deployment, so destroying it could hit another deployment's key.
rules.check: Check that tag or describe failures in listing code cause the key to be skipped, not counted as an orphan.

rules.statement: Automated KMS key destruction schedules a recoverable deletion or disables the key version, never an immediate purge.
rules.why: Every destruction must stay recoverable for the service's window in case a key was swept by mistake.
rules.check: Look for calls that purge or immediately delete keys (for example Azure purge, or deletion with no pending window) in automated destruction paths.

rules.statement: A port method that returns a large, I/O-backed listing streams results as IAsyncEnumerable<T> instead of returning a materialized collection.
rules.why: Listings like a provider's keys can be large and come from paged remote calls, so they are streamed.
rules.check: Look for new interface methods that return Task<List<T>> or arrays for unbounded remote or database listings.

rules.statement: A background job handler throws when a step it depends on (a listing or a read) fails, so that the dispatcher retries it, and is written so that running it again is harmless.
rules.why: Retries come from the dispatcher, so swallowing the failure loses the retry, and a repeated run must not cause damage.
rules.check: Check job handlers for caught-and-ignored failures in required reads and for side effects that are not idempotent when the job runs again.

rules.statement: Record audit events for destruction of KMS keys in the control-plane tenant, not the owning tenant's audit trail.
rules.why: The KMS key identifier must never reach a tenant's audit trail.
rules.check: Check audit events that carry KMS key identifiers for the tenant they are written to.
